newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT-NatWest trimmed at Salomon.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-NatWest trimmed at Salomon.

text.p: Earnings estimates for National Westminster Bank Plc were trimmed at Salomon Brothers, dealers said on Wednesday.
For the current year, Salomon analyst John Leonard said he cut his NatWest pre-tax profit estimate to 1.825 billion stg from 1.895 billion. For 1988, he cut to 2.055 billion stg from 2.125 billion.
In 1996 the company made pre-tax profits of 1.122 billion stg.

Leonard said the reductions followed a reassessment of NatWest's comments at its recent annual meeting, with margins seen under pressure in its UK banking business and expenses growing, especially due to technology investments.

On Tuesday, SocGen also lowered its NatWest earnings estimates, bringing its top-end figures in line with the market consensus, yet the outlook for the bank's shares is probably more tied up with recent talk of possible bids and mergers in the bank sector, dealers said.

NatWest has been seen as under pressure to do a deal, possibly with a domestic rival such as Abbey National Plc, to improve shareholder returns and tackle the recent underperformance of its shares, they said.
Leonard said he did not expect any merger news involving NatWest in the near term.
"Certainly the management is well aware of the issues...but I am not holding my breath for a big merger," Leonard said, who has maintained a "buy" recommendation on the stock.
NatWest shares were down 4p at 800 by 0952 GMT.
